name: Statute Drift
description: Data and code for the paper Section 302 No Longer Means Murder: Statute Drift in Open Language Models after India's Criminal-Code Replacement (submitted to ICCIDSDT-2027, Springer LNNS). On 1 July 2024 the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS) replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC), and nearly every offence was renumbered. This deposit holds: a benchmark of 407 offences whose IPC-to-BNS mapping two independent public sources agree on; 4,884 English and Hindi questions and 407 number-meaning multiple-choice items; every answer that 15 open-weight language models gave on 3 October 2026; seven repair runs (date line, law notice, BM25 retrieval, era-vector steering and three LoRA variants) on Qwen2.5-7B and Mistral-7B-v0.3; the rule-based answer parser and the Colab notebook that produced every result. Files statute_drift_offence_table_IPC_to_BNS.csv: the 407 cross-checked offences, with IPC and BNS sections and headings, collision/void kind and dev/test split. statute_drift_benchmark.zip: offences, questions and MCQs (Parquet and CSV), the 500-question MMLU slice, BNS titles, source disagreements and the Source A table. statute_drift_model_outputs.zip: for each model and repair, the raw and scored answers, forced-choice and letter log-probabilities, MMLU and era-probe outputs, and the run log.
